key_insight: Two-hidden-layer MLPs with ReLU-based activations can exactly reproduce piecewise polynomial finite element functions on simplicial meshes, including both discontinuous and continuous cases, without training.
engineering_relevance: This gives a constructive neural surrogate representation of FEM fields that preserves exact FE values and scales linearly with mesh size, making it useful for physics-informed surrogates, compression, and mesh-to-network conversion in solid mechanics.
method: First hidden layer uses ReLU^0 + ReLU to encode mesh-skeleton structure and piecewise support.
Second hidden layer uses degree-dependent ReLU^k to represent arbitrary polynomial degree exactly.
Parameters are computed directly from mesh geometry and finite element coefficients, with a half-open decomposition reducing width in the continuous case.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports exact representation for arbitrary polynomial degree and any spatial dimension, with parameter counts growing linearly in the number of elements and matching global degrees of freedom in the continuous case.
watch_item: The construction is exact but depends on structured mesh and finite element data, so implementation complexity and width can still grow with mesh topology and polynomial degree.
paper_title: Exact Representation of Piecewise Polynomial Finite Element Functions by Two-Hidden-Layer Multilayer Perceptrons
